messages:
devon: Heads up — noticed a lot of churn in gpu-preemptible pool in eu-west when training jobs finish. We're losing 5–10m while nodes are torn down and re-provisioned, driving higher costs and rollout flakiness. Thinking we should tune CA flags and nodepool TTL to: longer unneeded time, higher util threshold, priority expander. Anyone tried something that helped? :thinking:

maria: yup saw the same. Our observation: CA was killing nodes that had short lived pods/cron jobs. Increasing --scale-down-unneeded-time helped. Also set --scale-down-utilization-threshold to 0.25. Small wins.

alex: to add — we use expander=priority and give on-demand nodegroups lower priority (so CA packs onto preemptibles) but set a safety floor so at least 2 on-demand nodes are always present.

samir: fwiw we added --max-node-provision-time=15m and --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m. That reduced thrashing during scale-ups. Also annotated low-priority nodegroups with k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/node-group-priority: "50"

devon: can you paste the full args you used?

maria: sure —
```yaml
command:
  - ./cluster-autoscaler
  - --v=4
  - --cloud-provider=gce
  - --expander=priority
  - --scale-down-unneeded-time=30m
  - --scale-down-unready-time=20m
  - --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.25
  - --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
  - --max-node-provision-time=15m
  - --balance-similar-node-groups=true
```

samir: also recommend bumping eviction grace for gpu pods — add toleration + extended preStop to let checkpoints finish, or use PodDisruptionBudget on long-running jobs.

alex: good call. For cost: enable packing by setting NodeGroup priorities + set --expander=priority. Then reduce on-demand baseline to 2 nodes via minSize.

devon: thanks — we'll try that on staging. I'll also add a Job-level annotation to avoid CA evicting mid-checkpoint.

infra-bot: [deploy] cluster-autoscaler rollout started for staging at 1767780000

maria: nice. ping when staging run looks stable and we'll promote.

devon: will do, TY! :thumbsup:
